question.:question/problem:
Find the fundamental vector product of the surface generated by the vector-valued function

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\begin{pmatrix}u v\\u - v\\- v \sin{(u v )}\end{pmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The fundamental vector product is $\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v$, in that order. Hold the other parameter constant in each partial derivative.

Differentiate the coordinates to obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial}{\partial u}(u v)&=v\\\frac{\partial}{\partial u}(u - v)&=1\\\frac{\partial}{\partial u}(- v \sin{(u v )})&=- v^{2} \cos{(u v )}\\\frac{\partial}{\partial v}(u v)&=u\\\frac{\partial}{\partial v}(u - v)&=-1\\\frac{\partial}{\partial v}(- v \sin{(u v )})&=- u v \cos{(u v )} - \sin{(u v )}\end{aligned}
$$

The tangent vectors are

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=\begin{pmatrix}v\\1\\- v^{2} \cos{(u v )}\end{pmatrix},\\\mathbf r_v&=\begin{pmatrix}u\\-1\\- u v \cos{(u v )} - \sin{(u v )}\end{pmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Form the ordered determinant:

$$
\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\v & 1 & - v^{2} \cos{(u v )}\\u & -1 & - u v \cos{(u v )} - \sin{(u v )}\end{vmatrix}.
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v)_{1}&=(1)(- u v \cos{(u v )} - \sin{(u v )})\\&\quad -(- v^{2} \cos{(u v )})(-1)\\&=- u v \cos{(u v )} - v^{2} \cos{(u v )} - \sin{(u v )}.\end{aligned}
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v)_{2}&=-(v)(- u v \cos{(u v )} - \sin{(u v )})\\&\quad +(- v^{2} \cos{(u v )})(u)\\&=v \sin{(u v )}.\end{aligned}
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v)_{3}&=(v)(-1)\\&\quad -(1)(u)\\&=- u - v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{pmatrix}- u v \cos{(u v )} - v^{2} \cos{(u v )} - \sin{(u v )}\\v \sin{(u v )}\\- u - v\end{pmatrix}.
$$

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: \begin{pmatrix}- u v \cos{(u v )} - v^{2} \cos{(u v )} - \sin{(u v )}\\u v^{2} \cos{(u v )} + v \sin{(u v )}\\- v\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}- u v \cos{(u v )} - v^{2} \cos{(u v )} - \sin{(u v )}\\- v \sin{(u v )}\\- u - v\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}u v \cos{(u v )} + v^{2} \cos{(u v )} + \sin{(u v )}\\v \sin{(u v )}\\- u - v\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}- u v \cos{(u v )} - v^{2} \cos{(u v )} - \sin{(u v )}\\v \sin{(u v )}\\- u - v\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}u v \cos{(u v )} + v^{2} \cos{(u v )} + \sin{(u v )}\\- v \sin{(u v )}\\u + v\end{pmatrix}

question.:question/problem:
Find the fundamental vector product of the surface generated by the vector-valued function

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\begin{pmatrix}u v\\- v \cos{(u v )}\\- u + v\end{pmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The fundamental vector product is $\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v$, in that order. Hold the other parameter constant in each partial derivative.

Differentiate the coordinates to obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial}{\partial u}(u v)&=v\\\frac{\partial}{\partial u}(- v \cos{(u v )})&=v^{2} \sin{(u v )}\\\frac{\partial}{\partial u}(- u + v)&=-1\\\frac{\partial}{\partial v}(u v)&=u\\\frac{\partial}{\partial v}(- v \cos{(u v )})&=u v \sin{(u v )} - \cos{(u v )}\\\frac{\partial}{\partial v}(- u + v)&=1\end{aligned}
$$

The tangent vectors are

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=\begin{pmatrix}v\\v^{2} \sin{(u v )}\\-1\end{pmatrix},\\\mathbf r_v&=\begin{pmatrix}u\\u v \sin{(u v )} - \cos{(u v )}\\1\end{pmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Form the ordered determinant:

$$
\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\v & v^{2} \sin{(u v )} & -1\\u & u v \sin{(u v )} - \cos{(u v )} & 1\end{vmatrix}.
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v)_{1}&=(v^{2} \sin{(u v )})(1)\\&\quad -(-1)(u v \sin{(u v )} - \cos{(u v )})\\&=u v \sin{(u v )} + v^{2} \sin{(u v )} - \cos{(u v )}.\end{aligned}
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v)_{2}&=-(v)(1)\\&\quad +(-1)(u)\\&=- u - v.\end{aligned}
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v)_{3}&=(v)(u v \sin{(u v )} - \cos{(u v )})\\&\quad -(v^{2} \sin{(u v )})(u)\\&=- v \cos{(u v )}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{pmatrix}u v \sin{(u v )} + v^{2} \sin{(u v )} - \cos{(u v )}\\- u - v\\- v \cos{(u v )}\end{pmatrix}.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Find the fundamental vector product of the surface generated by the vector-valued function

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\begin{pmatrix}- u v\\u + v\\v e^{u v}\end{pmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The fundamental vector product is $\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v$, in that order. Hold the other parameter constant in each partial derivative.

Differentiate the coordinates to obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial}{\partial u}(- u v)&=- v\\\frac{\partial}{\partial u}(u + v)&=1\\\frac{\partial}{\partial u}(v e^{u v})&=v^{2} e^{u v}\\\frac{\partial}{\partial v}(- u v)&=- u\\\frac{\partial}{\partial v}(u + v)&=1\\\frac{\partial}{\partial v}(v e^{u v})&=u v e^{u v} + e^{u v}\end{aligned}
$$

The tangent vectors are

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u&=\begin{pmatrix}- v\\1\\v^{2} e^{u v}\end{pmatrix},\\\mathbf r_v&=\begin{pmatrix}- u\\1\\u v e^{u v} + e^{u v}\end{pmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Form the ordered determinant:

$$
\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v=\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\- v & 1 & v^{2} e^{u v}\\- u & 1 & u v e^{u v} + e^{u v}\end{vmatrix}.
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v)_{1}&=(1)(u v e^{u v} + e^{u v})\\&\quad -(v^{2} e^{u v})(1)\\&=u v e^{u v} - v^{2} e^{u v} + e^{u v}.\end{aligned}
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v)_{2}&=-(- v)(u v e^{u v} + e^{u v})\\&\quad +(v^{2} e^{u v})(- u)\\&=v e^{u v}.\end{aligned}
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}(\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v)_{3}&=(- v)(1)\\&\quad -(1)(- u)\\&=u - v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{pmatrix}u v e^{u v} - v^{2} e^{u v} + e^{u v}\\v e^{u v}\\u - v\end{pmatrix}.
$$

\begin{pmatrix}u v e^{u v} - v^{2} e^{u v} + e^{u v}\\v e^{u v}\\u - v\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}- u v e^{u v} + v^{2} e^{u v} - e^{u v}\\- v e^{u v}\\u - v\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}- u v e^{u v} + v^{2} e^{u v} - e^{u v}\\v e^{u v}\\u - v\end{pmatrix}
